verdict.rationale: Appwrite Functions can be triggered by server events, webhooks and scheduled executions, and run event handlers in isolated runtimes. That is a direct first-party mechanism for automatic actions on events. The evidence shows event-triggered code, but not a declarative rule layer with conditions or filters. It also lacks depth on which events are available and on independent validation. missing for 10: documented rule/condition definition (filtering which events fire which actions), event catalog and configuration detail, no-code rule authoring, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: These Functions can be triggered by HTTP requests, SDK methods, server events, webhooks, and scheduled executions.
Run API endpoints, webhooks, cron jobs, and event handlers in secure isolated runtimes that scale with demand.
Respond to server events in realtime.
